paragraphs: Rabbi Yose, son of Rav Chisda.
Mentioned in Zohar Chadash, Ruth, chapter 1: he spent the night on his father's grave. This is not Rav Chisda, the colleague of Rav Nachman, who was a priest, as explained in his entry.[^1][^2]

notes.text: אביו, “his father,” occurs twice consecutively in the supplied source and is rendered once. The cause of the duplication has not been established. The priestly Rav Chisda is explicitly distinguished from this man’s father.

The checked Zohar Chadash, Midrash Rut passage names Rabbi Chisda and Rabbi Yose his son, who spends the night at his grave. This supports the reported episode without establishing Hyman’s chapter label or his distinction from the priestly Rav Chisda. The doubled אביו remains preserved in the Hebrew; its cause is unknown. Hyman’s distinction and cross-reference remain his report, without an identity binding.
